precepts.text: Joseph's bones were buried in that parcel of ground at Shechem, and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph; the parcel of ground is the land of inheritance.
precepts.point: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.text: Choose you this day whom ye will serve. You cannot serve two masters. You cannot serve the flesh and serve God at the same time; you have to choose, and there is no in between. That is why he said, I would thou wert cold or hot: if you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, I will spue thee out of my mouth. But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
precepts.point: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption: you will be judged by it. But he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting: when you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord gives blessings, favor, mercy, and abundance.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

precepts.text: Everybody says they will serve the Lord — can you really examine that? You either rule the house the way Ephesians and Timothy lay it out, or the way the world taught you authority was.
precepts.point: A child counting the days until he can move out is a sentiment none of us should have in this truth, and the man responsible is the head of that house.

The others had doubt in them somewhere; these two had complete faith and never questioned what the Lord told Moses.

precepts.text: Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods; Laban came of that idolatrous house.
precepts.point: Jacob answered that he went away because he was afraid Laban would take his daughters from him by force, and said, With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

precepts.why:
“Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.” Terah and his house served other gods, and Laban was of the house of Nahor.

That is why Laban's question tells you what he was: “wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?” Laban was an idolater, just like his fathers on the other side of the flood. Jacob answered that he went away because he was afraid Laban would take his daughters from him by force, and, not knowing that Rachel had stolen them, said, “With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live”.

precepts.text: I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
precepts.point: I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat. Israel took over everything the nations had in those lands, the ships, the vineyards, the merchandise, and became the merchants of the land; it was theirs, because it was promised.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow.” This was promised long before: “And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.”

God was doing the fighting. Great nations bigger and more than Israel fell because the Most High was with them, not because of Israel's sword or bow. And because it was promised, everything those nations had in the land, the cities, the vineyards and oliveyards, the ships and the merchandise, was Israel's to dwell in and eat of; Israel became the merchants of the land.

precepts.text: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live, that thou mayest love the Lord thy God, obey his voice, and cleave unto him.
precepts.point: Moses said the same thing: he set life and death, blessing and cursing before Israel and said choose life. Deuteronomy 28 laid it out, blessings in verses 1 through 14 if Israel obeyed, to be above all people and rule; curses from 15 down to 68 if not. Israel chose the cursing and the death, and that is what we are in now, trying to come back and get out of it.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“choose you this day whom ye will serve”. Moses said the same thing: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days”.

Deuteronomy 28 laid it out: blessings in verses 1 through 14 if Israel obeyed, to be above all people and rule; curses from 15 down to 68 if not. Israel chose the cursing and the death, and that is what we are in now, trying to come back and get out of it.

A lot of people hang “as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord” up in the house and do not keep one law; everybody reads this verse and reads nothing before it about being put to death for going off. Choosing life means loving the Lord, obeying his voice and cleaving unto him. Lord willing they have space and time to repent.

precepts.text: All the people answered with one voice, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do; Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar and twelve pillars, read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, and sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people.
precepts.point: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the Lord.” It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then: “all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do.” Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar under the hill and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel, and read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, “and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient.”

Then the blood: half in basons, half sprinkled on the altar, and “Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

Joshua was Moses' successor and did the same thing at Shechem that his predecessor did at the mountain: the people in full agreement, witnesses against themselves, “The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey”, and a covenant made with a statute and an ordinance. We came into that covenant again, this time without the blood.

precepts.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun: Joshua and his father Nun were of the tribe of Ephraim.
precepts.point: They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in mount Ephraim; he is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
They buried Joshua “in the border of his inheritance in Timnath–serah, which is in mount Ephraim”. He is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father. That is in the list of the spies: “Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.”

Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, and his tribe is Ephraim. So his inheritance, and his grave, are in mount Ephraim.

precepts.text: As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
precepts.point: Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
Joshua said, “choose you this day whom ye will serve”, and then: “but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”

Eli did not hold his house to that. The man of God asked him, “Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?” That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. The Lord chose him “out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me”, and gave his father's house “all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel.” They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of.

“Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me”? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings.

Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way, but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.

precepts.text: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem: your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and the Most High took Abraham, multiplied his seed, and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt, where we served four hundred years.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem”: the elders, the heads, the judges and the officers, and “they presented themselves before God.”

Joshua rehearsed where we came from: “Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.” The Most High took Abraham from there, “multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac. And I gave unto Isaac Jacob and Esau”, and “Jacob and his children went down into Egypt”, where we served four hundred years.

Joshua warned us about the very thing Samuel faced. It was at Shechem that Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. So the Lord told Samuel, “According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.”

precepts.text: Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth, and put away the gods which your fathers served; if you are sincere about serving the Lord, you are going to keep the commandments.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the Lord.”

How do we serve the Lord in sincerity and in truth? If you are sincere about serving the Lord, you are going to keep the commandments. A lot of people today say they love the Lord, yet they do not do any of his commandments; they do not truly show they have the faith of Christ, because they do not keep the commandments.

Israel at Samuel's time had done the opposite: they “have forsaken me, and served other gods.”

precepts.text: Choose you this day whom ye will serve; but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“choose you this day whom ye will serve … but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”

A lot of us grew up with that plaque in the house, as for me and my house we will serve the Lord, and the house kept not one commandment: still eating pork, still keeping Sunday, still keeping the wicked pagan holidays of our oppressors.

Israel made its choice at Shechem. When they asked Samuel for a king, they were choosing again, and the Lord named it: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

precepts.text: The people answered, God forbid that we should forsake the Lord to serve other gods, for the Lord our God brought us up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; therefore will we also serve the Lord, for he is our God.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the Lord, to serve other gods.” They gave the reason with their own mouths: “the Lord our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and which did those great signs in our sight.” “therefore will we also serve the Lord; for he is our God.”

That is the very deliverance the Lord pointed to when he spoke to Samuel: “since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods.” The people who said God forbid we should forsake him are the people who forsook him. Asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

precepts.text: Joshua said, Ye cannot serve the Lord, for he is an holy God, he is a jealous God; if ye forsake the Lord and serve strange gods, he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“Ye cannot serve the Lord: for he is an holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins.”

Joshua warned them what would follow: “If ye forsake the Lord, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.”

That is the warning Israel walked past when it asked for a king. The Lord had done them good, bringing them up out of Egypt, and they rejected him “that I should not reign over them.”

precepts.text: The people said, Nay, but we will serve the Lord; ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord; the Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. We made that covenant.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the Lord.” Joshua made them witnesses: “Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.”

Then: “put away … the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto the Lord God of Israel. And the people said unto Joshua, The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.”

We made that covenant. So when the elders came to Samuel for a king, they were witnesses against themselves. The Lord told Samuel to “Hearken unto the voice of the people”, but they had sworn to obey his voice.

precepts.text: Fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth.
precepts.point: The true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth. Without temple, sacrifice or priesthood, a scattered people worship in sincerity and in truth, which is what Joshua charged Israel with.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
“But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. Joshua charged Israel with the same: “Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the Lord.”

Serve him in sincerity and in truth. Without temple, sacrifice or priesthood, a scattered people worship in sincerity and in truth, which is what Joshua charged Israel with. Salvation is of the Jews, because Christ sprang out of Judah; and the true worship is not tied to the mountain or to Jerusalem, but is in spirit and in truth, putting away the other gods and serving the Lord.

points: Therefore will we also serve the LORD; for he is our God.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua said unto the people, Ye cannot serve the LORD: for he is an holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: If ye forsake the LORD, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good. Everything he promised for good had come to pass and Israel was on top in the land; all they had to do was keep the commandments. Going off meant being taken out of that land into captivity, and because that is what Israel decided to do, that is the predicament we are in today.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: The people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the LORD. It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then; we came into that covenant again, this time without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua said, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him; and they said, We are witnesses. Everybody was in full agreement.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Put away the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto the LORD God of Israel; and the people said, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up under an oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us; for it hath heard all the words of the LORD which he spake unto us: it shall be therefore a witness unto you, lest ye deny your God.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: So Joshua let the people depart, every man unto his inheritance.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: After these things Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being an hundred and ten years old.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in mount Ephraim; he is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua, which had known all the works of the LORD that he had done for Israel.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver, and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Eleazar the son of Aaron died, and they buried him in a hill that pertained to Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim.
